European Commission (2009). Reference Document on Best Available Techniques for Energy Efficiency. Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control (IPPC), European IPPC Bureau, Joint Research Centre - Institute for Prospective Technological Studies, Seville, February 2009 (ENE BREF). No report number or DOI printed in the PDF.

Targeted pass of the 430-page horizontal Energy Efficiency BREF; data are EU-wide with some US DOE-derived worked examples. Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 32). Loaded (main file, 24 technologies in 33 process contexts): industrial heat pumps (compression COP and output temperature, absorption, MVR general COP and delivery temperature, Nymolla MVR capex), lithium bromide absorption chillers (COP), CHP default heat-to-power ratios (Table 3.20, Directive 2004/8/EC defaults), CHP type operating data, Bindewald engine CHP and Barajas trigeneration plants (efficiencies, capacity, capex), boiler efficiency worked examples (Siegert flue-gas loss, economiser 80 to 84.5 %), VSD drive loss, well-managed compressed air SEC (85-130 Wh/Nm3) and a plant example, fan peak efficiency, evaporator specific steam/electricity per tonne of water evaporated (Table 3.29), and superheated-steam drying. _measures (71 rows): savings versus existing practice for combustion, steam systems (economiser, scale, blowdown, traps, insulation, condensate and flash steam), heat recovery, motors, compressed air (Table 3.23 and the technique sections), pumps, ventilation/HVAC and drying, with the Annex 7.10 worked examples. _other-values: steam shares, dew points, shares of motor and compressed-air energy, Nymolla details, generic CHP efficiencies. No _flows file. Not loaded: lighting (out of scope), electrical power supply, transformers, power factor, energy-management and monitoring chapters, district cooling, chillers (refer to ICS BREF), BAT conclusions (Chapter 4 repeats Chapters 2-3 and prints no new numbers), CAES, benchmarking annexes. Traps: (1) the text layer loses dashes in ranges, so "6 7 %", "-4 50 %" and "20 80" are ranges 6-7, -4 to 50 and 20-80; the superheated-steam figure "6 70 kWh/t" has no dash on the rendered page and is read as 670 (latent heat 627 kWh/t); (2) Table 3.20 prints a power-to-heat ratio (unit mistyped as degC) - the main file stores the inverse as heat-to-power-ratio with formula; (3) Table 3.29 prints kg steam per tonne water evaporated with the kWh in brackets - the kWh was loaded; (4) Table 3.23 total 32.9 does not equal the sum of its contributions (38.1); (5) the 1 % per 20 degC and 1 % per 40 degC flue-gas rules both appear (pp.123/144 and p.145); (6) Annex boiler "745.7 W" is kW; (7) worked examples (Sect. 3.1.1.1, Annex 7.10.1) are illustrations with assumed inputs, not measurements; (8) few costs: no investment cost for boilers, heat pumps in general or motors; Nymolla and Bindewald capex carry no price year (publication year 2009 used and flagged) and Ford Solihull is quoted in 1991 prices. Lighting, ICS cooling and sector-specific processes are not covered by this horizontal BREF.
